kept.excerpt: As world leaders gather for the 81st United Nations General Assembly, Save the Children U.S. President and CEO Janti Soeripto is calling for greater urgency to protect children facing conflict, hunger and preventable disease. The Impact Alliance is a collaboration between Save the Children, CARE and Prosper Global designed to explore more connected, efficient and locally led delivery of humanitarian assistance. Soeripto is leading the organization’s U.S. delegation at UNGA81, focusing on child survival, nutrition, education and humanitarian diplomacy.
kept.relevance: This dated organizational statement documents current humanitarian activity and international advocacy relevant to the case for recognition.

kept.excerpt: In an interview with The National, Save the Children U.S. head Janti Soeripto described the trauma of displacement experienced by children in Lebanon as family members, friends and homes are lost. She said the UN humanitarian appeal for Lebanon was only 20 per cent funded. Soeripto planned to attend the UN General Assembly that week to appeal for support for children in conflict zones.
kept.relevance: Independent reporting close to the cutoff documents the organization’s public role in protecting children affected by war and the funding constraints facing that work.

kept.excerpt: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2020 Nobel Peace Prize to the World Food Programme for combating hunger, improving conditions for peace in conflict-affected areas and helping prevent hunger from being used as a weapon of war. The Committee emphasized that assistance to increase food security can improve prospects for stability and peace. It described the organization as playing a key role in multilateral cooperation.
kept.relevance: This official historical precedent shows that humanitarian relief in conflict zones and multilateral cooperation can satisfy the Committee’s conception of peace work.
